title: Sorting rules for different kinds of data
summary: Three rows compare the input and output when sorting integers in ascending order, English names lexicographically, and letter grades by a custom ranking from D to A+.
context: Each row starts with an unsorted input on the left. A right-pointing arrow gives the sorting rule, and the result appears on the right. The figure compares inputs and outputs without showing the algorithm’s internal steps.
description: Lexicographic order compares names character by character. Here the five names have different initials, so the first letter suffices. The custom grade ranking runs from low to high: D < C < B- < B < B+ < A < A+. It differs from ordinary ASCII lexicographic order. B-, B, and B+ are three distinct grades. The table gives the data for all three rows, from top to bottom.

frames.title: Sorting rules for different kinds of data
frames.explanation: Sorting changes only the order of the elements. The comparison rule determines the result.
